newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-BONALY COMEBACK COULD BE PREMATURE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-BONALY COMEBACK COULD BE PREMATURE.

text.p: Five-times champion Surya Bonaly won her fight last week to be included in the French team at the European figure skating championships but her performance in qualifying on Monday showed her comeback may have been premature.

Left out by the French Federation because they considered she was not fully recovered from an Achilles tendon injury, Bonaly won an appeal to be re-instated but on Monday managed only a lacklustre performance in her qualifying group.
Champion from 1991 to 1995, Bonaly finished a disappointing sixth in her group, won by Elena Liashenko of Ukraine.
"It was so-so. I think I can be better when it is more serious," she said.
"I was a bit scared and it was stupid to be scared for this because it was just a qualification. But it was difficult for me to be in good shape for this one.
"I have always been so confident but right now my confidence is only about 60 per cent."
The second group was dominated by the Russians, Maria Butyrskaya winning it from titleholder Irina Slutskaya with Olga Markova fourth. Vanessa Gusmeroli of France took third place.
Butyrskaya, Who had two of the day's best marks of 5.8 for artistry, declined to comment after her four-triple performance but the other two Russians dismissed the event as almost irrelevant.
"It was like a practice in front of judges. The real competition starts on Friday," Markova said.
Bonaly promised she would be working very hard ahead of Friday in an effort to overhaul the Russians. After five years as champion, she finished second to Slutskaya last year.
"Every day in practice has been better than the last," said Bonaly, who won her ninth French title in mid-December despite a display that led to the federation's decision to drop her.
"When I first came back, I could not do the flip or the lutz. But last week I got the lutz back," she said.
It was almost there on Monday, until it vanished in a two-footed landing and she completed only three triples in her routine, two toe loops and a salchow.
She messed up four other attempts.
"For me, qualification is a way to get fit again but it is difficult to perform your best programme," she said. "It was difficult to give your best for nothing."
The top 15 from each group went through to the main event.
Bonaly, a former gymnast, ruptured her right achilles tendon doing acrobatics last May.
Hers was a poor quality group, Liashenko, bronze medallist two years ago, winning it despite marks as low as 4.5 out of the maximum of 6.0. Her best was 5.4.
German Eva-Maria Fitze, 14, was a surprising second on her European debut with Yulia Vorobieva of Azerbaijan third.
